description: Lactarius subpurpureus is a medium-sized milk cap with a cap 3-10 cm across, convex at first, becoming flat to shallowly vase-shaped. The cap is zoned or spotted with wine-red and pale pink, fades to pinkish buff, and bruises green. The gills are attached to slightly decurrent, nearly distant, wine-red, and spot green when handled or with age. The stem is 3-8 cm long, colored like the cap or paler, sometimes pitted, and becomes hollow. The flesh is whitish to pink. KEY: scanty, deep wine-red latex that slowly stains green; taste mild to faintly peppery. Spore print pale cream.
habitat: Mycorrhizal with eastern hemlock and possibly other conifers, such as eastern white pine. Grows on the ground alone, scattered or in groups in conifer and mixed forests.
lookalikes: Lactarius paradoxus - also has wine-red latex, but its gills are putty-colored rather than wine-red
Lactarius deliciosus group - orange latex and orange cap that also stain green
safety_notes: EDIBILITY NOT CONFIRMED: The sources reviewed for this species do not assess its edibility. Identify it by the scanty deep wine-red latex and the green staining of the cap and gills. Do not eat any milk cap unless an expert has confirmed the identification.
